glycerin.description: Natural humectant that draws moisture into the skin. Very safe.

glycerol.description: Natural humectant, same as glycerin. Very safe.

methylparaben.description: Synthetic preservative. Known endocrine disruptor, linked to reproductive toxicity and breast cancer risk.

propylparaben.description: Strongest endocrine disruption among parabens. Linked to reproductive toxicity.

butylparaben.description: Strongest paraben. High endocrine disruption risk, found in breast tumors.

isobutylparaben.description: High endocrine disruption risk, banned in some countries.

fragrance.description: Undisclosed mixture of potentially thousands of chemicals. High risk of allergies, dermatitis, and endocrine disruption.

parfum.description: European term for undisclosed fragrance mixture. Same risks as 'fragrance'.

limonene.description: Citrus-derived fragrance. Can cause skin sensitization, especially oxidized.

sodium laureth sulfate.description: Ethoxylated surfactant. Can be harsh; may be contaminated with 1,4-dioxane (potential carcinogen).

sles.description: Abbreviation for Sodium Laureth Sulfate. Same risks.

sodium lauryl sulfate.description: Harsh surfactant. Strong skin and mucous membrane irritant. Can disrupt skin barrier.

sls.description: Abbreviation for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate. Same risks.

ammonium laureth sulfate.description: Similar to SLES but ammonium-based. Moderate irritation risk.

phenoxyethanol.description: Widely used preservative. Considered safer than parabens but can cause irritation and CNS effects in infants.

formaldehyde.description: Known carcinogen. Banned in many countries for cosmetics. Causes cancer, strong respiratory irritant.

dmdm hydantoin.description: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative. Releases formaldehyde slowly over time.

diazolidinyl urea.description: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative. Stronger than imidazolidinyl urea.

bronopol.description: Antimicrobial that releases formaldehyde and can form nitrosamines.

triclosan.description: Antimicrobial agent. Endocrine disruptor, contributes to antibiotic resistance. Banned in OTC antibacterials by FDA.

phthalates.description: Group of chemicals used as plasticizers. Strong endocrine disruptors, linked to birth defects.

dibutyl phthalate.description: Known reproductive toxicant. Banned in cosmetics in EU.

diethyl phthalate.description: Common nail polish plasticizer. Suspected endocrine disruptor.

retinol.description: Vitamin A derivative. Effective anti-aging but can cause severe irritation, peeling, and sun sensitivity. Not safe during pregnancy.

retinyl palmitate.description: Vitamin A ester. Concerns about photocarcinogenicity when applied to sun-exposed skin.

hydroquinone.description: Skin bleaching agent. Potential carcinogen, causes ochronosis with long-term use. Banned in OTC products in EU.

mercury.description: Highly toxic heavy metal. Neurotoxic, nephrotoxic. Found in some skin-lightening creams. Completely banned in cosmetics.

lead.description: Toxic heavy metal. Neurotoxic. Found as contaminant in some lipsticks.

aluminum.description: Used in antiperspirants. Suspected neurotoxin and estrogen mimicker. Debate ongoing.

benzophenone.description: UV absorber. Potential endocrine disruptor. Photoallergic reactions reported.

oxybenzone.description: Chemical UV filter. Strong endocrine disruptor. Absorbed into bloodstream. Harmful to coral reefs.

octinoxate.description: Chemical UV filter. Endocrine disruptor, absorbed through skin.

titanium dioxide.description: Physical UV blocker. Generally safe in topical use. Inhalation of nanoparticles is concerning.

zinc oxide.description: Physical UV blocker. Generally considered safe. Broad-spectrum protection.

mineral oil.description: Petroleum-derived oil. Creates occlusive layer on skin. Refined versions are safe; poorly refined can be carcinogenic.

petrolatum.description: Petroleum jelly. Can be contaminated with PAHs (carcinogens) if not fully refined.

paraffin.description: Petroleum-derived wax. Same concerns as mineral oil.

silica.description: Silicon dioxide. Generally safe in cosmetics. Inhalation risk if airborne.

dimethicone.description: Silicone polymer. Generally considered safe but occlusive. Can cause buildup on skin and hair.

cyclomethicone.description: Cyclic silicone. Bioaccumulates in environment. Under regulatory review.

cyclopentasiloxane.description: Cyclic silicone (D5). Environmental bioaccumulation concerns. Restricted in EU for wash-off products.

propylene glycol.description: Humectant and penetration enhancer. Can cause irritation and allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

butylene glycol.description: Milder than propylene glycol. Generally well-tolerated.

polyethylene glycol.description: PEG compounds. Can be contaminated with 1,4-dioxane. Penetration enhancers that increase absorption of other chemicals.

peg-.description: Polyethylene glycol compound. Can be contaminated with 1,4-dioxane.

talc.description: Mineral powder. Risk of contamination with asbestos fibers. Inhalation risk. FDA investigating ovarian cancer link.

coal tar.description: Known carcinogen. Used in dandruff/psoriasis treatments. Banned in cosmetics in EU.

bha.description: Butylated Hydroxyanisole. Possible human carcinogen (IARC Group 2B). Endocrine disruptor.

butylated hydroxyanisole.description: Same as BHA. Possible carcinogen and endocrine disruptor.

bht.description: Butylated Hydroxytoluene. Possible carcinogen. Some concern for endocrine disruption.

butylated hydroxytoluene.description: Same as BHT. Preservative with carcinogen concern.

sodium hydroxide.description: Lye/caustic soda. Used in tiny amounts to adjust pH. Safe at low concentrations in final product.

citric acid.description: Natural acid from citrus. Generally safe. Can cause mild irritation in high concentrations.

niacinamide.description: Vitamin B3. Excellent skin brightener, reduces pores, anti-inflammatory. Very well-tolerated.

hyaluronic acid.description: Naturally occurring molecule. Excellent hydration. Very safe for all skin types.

sodium hyaluronate.description: Salt form of hyaluronic acid. Penetrates skin more effectively.

ceramide.description: Naturally present in skin. Repairs skin barrier. Extremely safe.

peptide.description: Amino acid chains. Signal proteins for skin repair. Generally very safe.

vitamin c.description: L-Ascorbic acid. Powerful antioxidant and brightener. Can cause irritation at high concentrations.

tocopherol.description: Vitamin E. Powerful antioxidant. Generally safe and beneficial.

tocopheryl acetate.description: Vitamin E ester. Stable form of Vitamin E. Very safe.

aloe vera.description: Soothing plant extract. Very safe. Excellent for sensitive skin.

aloe barbadensis.description: Scientific name for aloe vera. Very safe.

green tea extract.description: Polyphenol-rich antioxidant. Very safe and beneficial.

chamomile extract.description: Soothing anti-inflammatory botanical. Safe for most; ragweed allergy cross-reaction possible.

shea butter.description: Natural plant butter. Excellent emollient. Very safe.

jojoba oil.description: Liquid wax from jojoba plant. Closely mimics skin sebum. Very safe.

argan oil.description: Moroccan oil. Rich in vitamin E and fatty acids. Very safe.

coconut oil.description: Natural oil. Very moisturizing but highly comedogenic (pore-clogging) for acne-prone skin.

squalane.description: Plant-derived hydrocarbon. Lightweight, non-comedogenic emollient. Excellent safety profile.

rosehip oil.description: Rich in vitamin C and A. Beneficial but can oxidize. Generally safe.

ethanol.description: Alcohol. Can be drying and irritating with repeated use. Denatures protective skin proteins.

alcohol denat.description: Denatured alcohol. Same concerns as ethanol, plus added denaturing agents.

isopropyl alcohol.description: Rubbing alcohol. Drying, irritating, and disrupts skin barrier with regular use.

cetyl alcohol.description: Fatty alcohol from coconut. Emollient and thickener. Not drying like regular alcohol.

stearyl alcohol.description: Fatty alcohol. Emollient and thickener. Safe.

cetearyl alcohol.description: Mixture of cetyl and stearyl alcohol. Emollient. Safe.

benzyl alcohol.description: Can be irritating in some individuals. Safe at low concentrations.

salicylic acid.description: Beta-hydroxy acid. Effective acne treatment. Can cause dryness and sun sensitivity.

glycolic acid.description: Alpha-hydroxy acid exfoliant. Effective but increases sun sensitivity.

lactic acid.description: Gentle AHA exfoliant. Milder than glycolic acid. Good for sensitive skin.

azelaic acid.description: Naturally derived acid. Treats acne and rosacea. Well-tolerated.

zinc pyrithione.description: Anti-dandruff agent. Effective but has environmental toxicity concerns.

selenium sulfide.description: Anti-dandruff agent. Can cause hair discoloration and irritation.

ketoconazole.description: Antifungal agent for dandruff. Generally safe but some hormonal effects at high systemic doses.

coumarin.description: Fragrance ingredient. Potential carcinogen, liver toxic, restricted in EU.

musk.description: Synthetic musk compounds. Can bioaccumulate and are potential endocrine disruptors.

polysorbate 20.description: Ethoxylated sorbitol ester. Can be contaminated with 1,4-dioxane.

carbomer.description: Synthetic polymer used as thickener and stabilizer. Generally safe.

sodium benzoate.description: Preservative that can form benzene (carcinogen) when combined with vitamin C in acidic environment.

potassium sorbate.description: Generally regarded as safe preservative derived from sorbic acid.

artificial color.description: Synthetic dyes. Some linked to hyperactivity, carcinogenicity. Specific risk depends on dye.

red 40.description: Synthetic red dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children. Possible allergen.

yellow 5.description: Tartrazine. Common allergen, especially in aspirin-sensitive individuals.

blue 1.description: Brilliant Blue FCF. Potential carcinogen at high doses in animal studies.

monosodium glutamate.description: MSG. Flavor enhancer. Controversial; some report sensitivity symptoms though large studies inconclusive.

trans fat.description: Industrially produced trans fatty acids. Strongly linked to cardiovascular disease.

high fructose corn syrup.description: Processed sweetener. Linked to obesity, metabolic syndrome, and fatty liver disease.

aspartame.description: Artificial sweetener. Not safe for phenylketonurics (PKU). IARC classified as possible carcinogen (Group 2B) in 2023.

sucralose.description: Artificial sweetener (Splenda). Changes gut microbiome. Potential gut dysbiosis.

saccharin.description: Oldest artificial sweetener. Once thought carcinogenic; removed from carcinogen list. Still controversial.

sodium nitrite.description: Meat preservative. Converts to nitrosamines (carcinogens) during cooking. Linked to colorectal cancer.

sodium nitrate.description: Similar to sodium nitrite. Preserved meat additive.

bha food.description: Butylated hydroxyanisole used as food preservative. Possible carcinogen.
